title: JSON call validation playbook and runtime error guidance
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a playbook that specifies a compact, opinionated JSON-schema style for tool/function call contracts, a topology for runtime validation (compile-time + preflight + runtime), error class taxonomy, and deterministic recovery strategies. The deliverable is a single-page developer guide + runtime checklist + a small library patch that implements the canonical error codes and a lenient coercion shim for legacy tools.

Context and motivation:
- Multiple teams have implemented slight variants of tool parameter checks which produce inconsistent errors and poor UX for SDK users.
- Customers integrating function/tool calling report confusing validation failures (no clear next steps, spurious 500s).
- We must standardize for hosted, dedicated, and private modes while preserving extensibility for legacy/third-party tools.

Goals:
1) Define a minimal schema subset we ship as the canonical "call contract" syntax (enforceable in runtime).
2) Provide a taxonomy of validation errors with stable machine-friendly codes and user-friendly messages.
3) Design runtime behaviors for strict, permissive, and shimmed compatibility modes and when to fall back to model-side best-effort.
4) Add observability hooks and metrics to track validation rejections, coercions, and shim invocations.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing full JSON Schema support in tooling. This ticket focuses on the subset we guarantee across all runtimes and the mapping to error messages.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (developer-facing) describing the canonical syntax, examples, and migration patterns.
- RFC-style decision log for core tradeoffs.
- Implementation note + small reference lib change with tests.
- API surface: new header "X-Call-Contract-Version" and runtime config flag "validation_mode" (strict|permissive|compat_shim).
acceptance_criteria:
- A one-page playbook added to docs repo with canonical contract examples and migration steps.
- Runtime accepts the canonical subset and returns documented error codes for the cases below.
- Metrics emitted: validation.rejected, validation.coercions, validation.shim_applied with labels (route, model, contract_version).
- E2E test demonstrating a shim path that transforms legacy shape -> canonical shape and logs shim_applied.
- Security review signoff for the compat_shim behavior (only allowed for non-sensitive parameter families).
technical_details:
Canonical contract subset:
- Supported keywords: type, properties, required, enum, minLength, maxLength, minimum, maximum, format (email,date-time), examples.
- Disallowed/ignored: patternProperties, dependencies, $ref (no remote refs in runtime), additionalItems.
- AdditionalProperties default: false unless explicitly set to true.
- Examples and description fields are recommended for runtime hinting but not required.

Validation pipeline:
1) Compile-time: schema linting during CI (validate keys, check examples present for public contracts, fingerprint contract).
2) Preflight: on first deploy or contract change, runtime compiles schema into validator and stores fingerprint in contract metadata.
3) Runtime: incoming call -> if fingerprint mismatch reject with CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH (client action: rebind contract). Else validate input.

Validation modes and behavior:
- strict: reject on type/value mismatch with VALIDATION_REJECTED and human-friendly message.
- permissive: attempt coercion (strings->numbers, trim strings, parse booleans) and return VALIDATION_COERCED when successful. Coercions are deterministic and logged.
- compat_shim: run a lightweight shape-adaptor (field renames, nested flatten/unflatten for known legacy patterns) then validate. If adapt fails -> VALIDATION_REJECTED. Shim usage restricted by contract flag "allow_compat_shim: true".

Error taxonomy (machine_code | http_status | short_description | user_action):
- VALIDATION_REJECTED | 400 | input failed validation | review contract and payload
- VALIDATION_COERCED | 200 | input coerced to canonical shape | verify values and update client if necessary
- CONTRACT_VERSION_MISMATCH | 409 | contract/fingerprint mismatch | update client binding
- SHIM_APPLIED | 200 | compatibility shim transformed payload | monitor shim count and migrate clients
- MALFORMED_JSON | 400 | invalid JSON syntax | fix payload JSON formatting
- TOOL_INVOCATION_ERROR | 500 | runtime/tool failed post-validation | see logs and PR for the tool implementation

Observation and metrics:
- Emit counters and histograms with tags: route, model, client_sdk_version, contract_version, validation_mode, error_code.
- Include sample Grafana panels in docs: validation reject rate, coercion ratio, shim usage over time.

Migration guidance for SDKs:
- Add opt-in header X-Validation-Mode for clients. Default is "strict" on new contracts.
- Provide an SDK helper that performs local pre-validation to surface errors before network call.

Runtime safety constraints:
- Compat shim can only mutate non-credential fields (rule: any field labeled "sensitive": true in schema cannot be coerced or shimmed).
- Avoid silent coercion of enums; enum coercions must be explicit and logged.

Documentation artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Call+Contract+Playbook (draft)
- Reference PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4829 (WIP)
- Migration checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/migration-calls-playbook.pdf
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Chose a conservative JSON subset to guarantee consistent runtime behavior across hosted/dedicated/private - tradeoff: restricts some expressive schema patterns.
Provide explicit compat_shim instead of automatic heuristics to reduce silent data corruption - tradeoff: requires clients to opt-in for leniency.
Expose coercion metrics and require logging to track downstream quality regressions - tradeoff: additional telemetry cost but necessary for customer debugging.
